slides.title: Model Capacity Frontier: A Development Framework for LLM-Supported Social Simulation
slides.highlight: This paper introduces the Model Capacity Frontier (MCF) framework to systematically navigate the open-ended design space of LLM-supported agent-based models, demonstrating how architectural refinements can balance competing performance metrics in large-scale crowd simulations.

card.one_liner: Model Capacity Frontier framework evaluates LLM-supported agent-based models across configurations to distinguish architectural limits from tuning issues.
card.key_idea: Characterizes attainable empirical performance via Pareto frontiers across admissible configurations, guiding iterative architectural refinement in open-ended LLM-ABM design spaces.
card.evaluation: Validated on 12,000-agent crowd simulation using video-derived temporal, spatial, and flow metrics; compares conventional vs. LLM-enhanced architectures via matched configurations.
card.limitation: High computational cost for LLM evaluations limits configuration sampling; results depend on defining admissible parameter spaces and separating architecture from configuration.

slides.title: Gossip Agents: Reputation through Opinion Dynamics over Evolving Networks
slides.highlight: This work models reputation diffusion through gossip and opinion dynamics in evolving networks, offering insights into how information propagation mechanisms influence cooperation in multi-agent systems relevant to MIMIC's societal-scale simulations.

card.one_liner: Reputation diffusion via gossip over dynamic networks promotes cooperation and sustainability in multi-agent social dilemmas.
card.key_idea: Agents form private opinions from observations, exchange them via DeGroot dynamics over evolving networks, and aggregate them into reputation signals.
card.evaluation: Tested in n-player Prisoner's Dilemma and Harvest gridworlds using DQN; compared against no-reputation baselines across varying broadcast radii.
card.limitation: Relies on fixed, hand-crafted assessment rules for prosocial/antisocial behavior rather than learned evaluation policies.

slides.title: PRIMA: Pose Refined Inductive Motion Adapter for Zero Shot Social Bodily Behavior Recognition
slides.tldr: POSE-GUIDED VLM ADAPTER FOR ZERO-SHOT SOCIAL BEHAVIOR
slides.highlight: PRIMA introduces a lightweight adapter that injects body-structure priors into frozen Vision-Language Models to recognize fine-grained social bodily behaviors like postural shifts and backchanneling without requiring pose input at inference. This approach supports HyECHO's goal of efficient multimodal social perception by enabling zero-shot adaptation to new behavior taxonomies and improving correlations with human ratings of rapport and dominance.

card.one_liner: PRIMA injects pose-guided body-structure priors into frozen VLMs for zero-shot transfer across behavior taxonomies.
card.key_idea: Lightweight adapter aligns RGB features with pose-informed teacher features during training, enabling RGB-only inference and cross-backbone reuse.
card.evaluation: Zero-shot tests on MMA 52, BBSI, and NTU RGB+D 120 using Qwen3 VL and InternVL3.5; significant gains over baselines.
card.limitation: Struggles with fine hand details and temporal trajectories; performance depends on pose estimation quality and indoor dataset scope.

slides.title: Towards Adaptive and Real-Survey-Aligned Simulated Urban Mobility Behaviour of Generative Agents
slides.highlight: This study evaluates generative agents for simulating multimodal urban mobility, demonstrating their ability to handle unforeseen events and align with real survey data, which is relevant to MIMIC's goal of modeling complex human-AI societal interactions.

card.one_liner: Generative agents match survey modal splits but fail individual trip accuracy, though they adapt to unforeseen events.
card.key_idea: Simulates multimodal mobility using LLM-based agents with tuned prompts, comparing them against discrete choice models and baselines.
card.evaluation: Tested on 3,299 trips from a French household survey using 15 decision-makers, measuring modal split divergence and trip-level accuracy.
card.limitation: High computational cost and poor individual trip realism despite good aggregate modal splits; prompt tuning relies on survey data.

slides.title: Context Matters! Social, Spatial, and Semantic Coordination with an Embodied Agent in Immersive Analytics
slides.highlight: This paper proposes a framework for context-aware embodied agents in AR, focusing on spatial, social, and semantic coordination, which aligns with RwB's interest in human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: Proposes a context-aware framework for embodied AI agents in immersive analytics, demonstrated via the Cobot design probe.
card.key_idea: Conceptualizes context via spatial, social, and semantic dimensions, split into embeddedness and awareness, to guide embodied agent design.
card.evaluation: Qualitative reflection on the Cobot design probe using hypothetical use-case scenarios; lacks empirical user studies or quantitative metrics.
card.limitation: Framework is preliminary and single-user focused; relies on informal testing and hypothetical scenarios rather than rigorous empirical validation.

slides.title: GCAM-Gym: A Benchmark for Agent-Based Climate Policy Search
slides.highlight: This paper introduces GCAM-Gym, a Gymnasium-compatible environment for evaluating agent-based climate policy search methods, providing a standardized benchmark for comparing control systems under various feedback and budget constraints.

card.one_liner: GCAM-Gym benchmarks climate policy search methods using a standardized interface for the GCAM simulator.
card.key_idea: A Gymnasium-compatible environment for GCAM supporting full-policy and stepwise control, with structured observations and attempt-budgeted evaluation.
card.evaluation: Compared seven systems (e.g., CMA-ES, BO, PPO) across three settings using 3,210 GCAM evaluations; CMA-ES achieved highest IQM returns.
card.limitation: Results rely on a single GCAM configuration with unvalidated monetary units and documented runtime defects affecting temperature readouts.

slides.title: Persona AI Brings Calm Experience to Humanoid Startups
slides.highlight: This funding news highlights the growing market for humanoid robots, which aligns with RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Text Dominance in Paralinguistic Conflict: Tracing Suppression Through Audio LLM Circuits
slides.highlight: This study reveals that audio LLMs often prioritize transcript content over acoustic cues like emotion and speaker identity, a limitation relevant to HyECHO's goal of robust multimodal social perception. The findings highlight the need for mechanisms that effectively integrate paralinguistic signals to accurately model human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: Audio LLMs heavily prioritize text over acoustic cues, with suppression mechanisms traced via circuit analysis.
card.key_idea: Quantifies text dominance in six audio LLMs and uses probing, back-patching, and attention knockout to trace suppression circuits.
card.evaluation: Tested six models on LISTEN-style conflicts; mean text dominance 0.78. Used mechanistic interpretability tools; results public on GitHub.
card.limitation: Back-patching replication failed, limiting mechanistic conclusions; effects absent in multiple-choice benchmarks, hiding issues in standard evaluations.

slides.title: Sensitivity Analysis of Decision Rules in an Agent-Based Agro-Ecological Model
slides.highlight: This work introduces a method for sensitivity analysis in agent-based models with hierarchical decision structures, relevant to MIMIC for modeling complex, multi-scale societal systems where agent choices are conditional and branched.

card.one_liner: Proposes a hierarchical sensitivity analysis method for agent-based agro-ecological models with conditional parameters.
card.key_idea: Encodes crop decisions as a hierarchical graph and uses random-forest-supervised HSIC-ANOVA to rank effects without imputing inactive variables.
card.evaluation: Applied to MAELIA platform (5,000 simulations, winter wheat) analyzing nitrogen leaching, soil carbon, and yield against standard flat-space biases.
card.limitation: Requires extensive expert knowledge to define valid hierarchical structures and computationally intensive for high-order interactions.

slides.title: Machina Pauliana: A neuro-symbolic approach to the actio pauliana in Dutch insolvency law
slides.highlight: This paper demonstrates a neuro-symbolic architecture for legal reasoning, combining symbolic rule-based logic with neural case-based retrieval, which aligns with MIMIC's use of neuro-symbolic agent models for complex societal simulations.

card.one_liner: Neuro-symbolic model for Dutch insolvency law combines Catala rules with LLM-based case retrieval.
card.key_idea: Symbolic Catala solver handles logic; neural routines extract facts and resolve open-textured terms via RAG over Dutch judgments.
card.evaluation: Tested on 10 hand-annotated cases; segmentation/labelling high precision/recall; end-to-end F1 ~0.72-0.77, struggles with knowledge requirement.
card.limitation: Small, biased validation set of hard cases; retrieval depth shows no clear quantitative gain; knowledge requirement remains weak.

slides.title: YYForce Brings Humanoid Robots to Hospitality in Landmark Partnership with Novotel & Mercure Singapore on Stevens
slides.highlight: This partnership demonstrates the practical deployment of humanoid robots in hospitality settings, offering insights into human-robot interaction in service environments relevant to embodied social robotics.

slides.title: Moss Intelligence raises $149M Pre-A for real-time multimodal AI
slides.highlight: Moss Intelligence secured $149M in a Pre-A round to advance real-time multimodal AI, a capability relevant to the hybrid human-AI team state perception goals of HyECHO.

slides.title: Honeyed Words, Hidden Daggers: Benchmarking and Training LLMs to See Through Mock Politeness
slides.highlight: This work introduces a benchmark and training method for detecting mismatches between polite surface forms and hostile underlying intents, directly supporting HyECHO's goal of modeling group norms and engagement in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: Introduces ZhenhuanBench and CPR-GRPO to train small LLMs to detect mock politeness using expert annotations.
card.key_idea: Constructs a theory-grounded benchmark from expert commentary and trains models via Annotation-Grounded Verifiable Rewards and chance-corrected GRPO.
card.evaluation: Assessed on 1,592 items across 34 LLMs; an 8B model reaches 67.0 MCQ accuracy, surpassing GPT-5 on specific tasks.
card.limitation: Data derives from a single Chinese drama, risking domain bias and potential overlap with model pretraining corpora.

slides.title: LaMER: Language-Conditioned Multi-Expert Routing for Weakly Supervised Referring Expression Comprehension
slides.tldr: WEAKLY SUPERVISED REC VIA MULTI-EXPERT ROUTING
slides.highlight: This work addresses Referring Expression Comprehension, a capability explicitly noted as underpinning human-robot interaction, by proposing a weakly supervised framework that dynamically aggregates visual encoders based on language cues.

card.one_liner: LaMER uses language-conditioned multi-expert routing to achieve state-of-the-art weakly supervised referring expression comprehension.
card.key_idea: Aggregates four frozen visual experts via a language-conditioned cross-modal routing fusion module and cell-text matching head with negative anchor augmentation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, and RefCOCOg using Acc@IoU≥0.5; outperforms DViN and WeakMCN by up to 16.49 points with ablation validation.
card.limitation: Relies on four frozen expert encoders, potentially increasing inference overhead and computational cost compared to single-backbone methods.
